governance.note: caiso-48 carries the caiso-45 stack verbatim (caiso-42 keeper levers + the caiso-44 startup-cost-aware RA bridge + the caiso_bidir_intertie export sink) and adds ONE control: caiso_ra_bridge_decommit, the solar-proportional / seasonal decommitment on the startup bridge. Both of its components are unit-commitment physics, not fits: (1) economic bridges are bounded to the 24-hour day-ahead commitment horizon (DA_COMMITMENT_HORIZON_HOURS; CAISO IFM/RUC commit one operating day — a longer idle is a next-day decommit/re-offer, never an intra-day min-load hold), and (2) gap hours where the candidate min-load floors exceed the model's OWN P1 dispatchable absorption (import-tranche dispatch that can back down + unused export-sink capacity) reprice the held energy to the curtailable-renewable keep-running offer (-renewable_keep_running_value, the constant the negative-offer dispatch already uses), and uneconomic bridges decommit cheapest-startup-first (the RUC de-commitment order; monotone, no iteration). Every input is the model's own P1 solution plus physical constants (startup cost, min-down, DA horizon, the existing renewable offer floor) — no adder/haircut/sigmoid tuned to a residual, no unit pinned to observed generation, no input rescaled to land on actuals. All carried levers trace to measured inputs as attested for caiso-42 (CAMPD net-load-filtered outage windows, F923 delivered gas + hub-basis overlay, EIA-930 priced interchange + 3-yr p95 forward-ATC envelope, EIA-930 monthly hydro budget, CAMPD-measured 0.26 CC minimum stable load, EIA-930-measured 3.5 GW export peak).
governance.model_miss_note: All deciding fails are genuine MODEL MISSes; none is ledgered. KEY FINDING (refutes the caiso-45 open item 'the bridge over-commits gas in high-solar years'): the bridge's net annual-gas effect is +0.58 / -0.88 / +0.14 TWh (P2 minus P1, 2023/24/25) — the caiso-45 2025 '+34.4% over EIA-923' guardrail trip was the P1 BASELINE measured against the raw PRELIMINARY 2025 EIA-923 vintage (55.2 TWh, 132.6 TWh total vs EIA-930's 186.4 — ~71% reporting); on the verdict machinery's repaired basis the 2025 gas overhang is +7.9% (C2 FAIL, improved from caiso-42's +12.3%) and it exists BEFORE any floor is applied. The decommit control is correspondingly quiet in-sample: the surplus screen rarely binds because P1 import dispatch plus the 3.5 GW export-sink headroom exceed the candidate min-load floors in nearly every gap hour, and the DA-horizon cap removes only the rare multi-day bridges the plain restart inequality already rejected. The 2024 negative-price hours (148) are present already at P1 — they come from the export sink + negative renewable offers + solar depth, not from bridged commitment; 2023/2025 negatives (25/32) appear only at P2, where the bridge floors create the marginal midday surplus. Remaining misses: C1 CC_REGULAR over-dispatch (2023 +8.51 / 2024 +11.10 TWh — worse than caiso-42's +9.21 because the bidir-intertie baseline raises CC infra-marginality; the midday-import / solar-glut merit wedge, not the bridge), the C3a/b body overprice (+54.9/+39.8/+45.4% mean; the structural CA gas+CARB SRMC floor above the import-/hydro-marginal actual), the C3c tails (2023 161h vs 21h >$200 — entirely the calibrated 7,500 MW WECC_import simultaneous cap, the separate reconciled-seam-limit thread; 2024/25 0h vs 35/8h — the model still lacks the real scarcity events), C4 2025 gas dispatch r=0.494 (improved from 0.416), and C5a CO2 (2024 +10.6%, 2025 +8.4% — tracks the gas volume wedge). NOT PROMOTED: registered as a probe; the caiso-42 keeper stands. Next structural lever per this finding: the 2025 gas overhang and the CC_REGULAR wedge are P1 merit-order properties (import tranche prices / CC offer curves / hub coupling), and the 2023 tail needs the reconciled WECC seam limit (rule #12).
